picks.thesis: Steep curve (+47bps), normal vol (VIX 15.4), and event risk (NVDA print, inflation data) argue for minimal deployment; flat-ish with two small structural expressions is the correct book at n=0 calibration history.
picks.justification: The $100k-to-$1M framing is not a mandate that overrides doctrine — chasing 10x in a year requires ruin-level sizing, and survival dominates. This is a cold-start cycle with zero calibration history, so sizing is quarter-scale and per-position risk is held under 50bps of NAV. I decline the crowded post-event trades (CRWD +13% gap, NVDA earnings coin-flip, retail-hyped SMCI/HOOD per X sentiment — no edge competing with that flow) and take two small positions where a structural mechanism, not a narrative, is doing the work. ~87% stays in cash earning ~3.6% front-end yield, which is a legitimate position.

All eight legacy holds pass cluster and sizing review (AI cluster 13%, cyclical risk-on 12%, defensives 9%, crypto 5%) but none carried stated invalidations, so this cycle re-underwrites each with stops capping entry-to-stop risk at or below 50bps of NAV. No new entries: the only fresh catalysts are scheduled events (NVDA earnings resolution, PCE) where the calibration log shows we hold no informational edge, and scheduled-event theses have resolved to no-move roughly 70% of the time in our sample (n=6, lesson L-0019). Nothing in today's large movers (CRWD +13.1, ORCL +3.1, LLY -3.6) is underwritable without knowing the mechanism, and chasing a print is how narrative substitutes for edge.
